summary.rule: Complete and verified = claimed tested AND named test exists and passed AND independent verdict VERIFIED. Unverified, blocked and owner-decision items stay in the denominator.

namedTests.name: custom expressions follow the authoring policy, results enter the hash, rule-free templates keep theirs

independentVerification.note: Three levels exist (catalog scorers, Registry.Presets, typed ScoreExpr interpreted by precompiled F#); the named test asserts policy blocker POLICY-CUSTOM-EXPRESSION, undeclared-capability blocker, and that results enter the template hash with a pinned golden hash. Source text is mostly SHOULD-level architecture.

namedTests.name: a template using every case reads back unchanged, with every overall scoring

gaps: §10 'incompatible operand types' / 'references to unavailable answer values': Expression.check (Expression.fs:173) only checks that an Item's question exists, not that it yields a number; an Item over a multi-choice, ranking or unscored-option question passes publication and silently evaluates as missing (Template.keyedNumber falls to Primitives.numeric -> None).
The named test (TemplateDecodeTests:251) only checks a round-trip and would not fail if validation or limits regressed; the real validation test is ScoringAstTests:97.
§11 limits on conditional nesting and aggregation size are not implemented (only depth, node count and referenced items). The source lists these as 'possible', so this is minor.
independentVerification.note: Numeric and boolean expressions are separate types, evaluation is pure over a constrained Env, and the version, reference, zero-divisor, empty-aggregate and depth/node limits are checked and tested. Operand-type checks for item references are missing. Custom scoring is overall-only, so circular section dependencies do not apply.

namedTests.name: non-numeric answers are left out of the mean, never counted as zero

gaps: Named test exercises only the legacy pilot Assessment module's missing-answer exclusion, not the registry; registry identities are tested in ScoringAstTests:230
Every scorer identity is hard-coded Version = 1 (Registry.fs:45-47); versioning is nominal, no v2 dispatch path exists yet
Missing policy offers only Exclude/Substitute + minimum observations; 'prohibit until complete'/'provisional' are not distinct options (source lists them as 'possible')
independentVerification.note: Source statements are 'should'-level architecture guidance; registry, explicit missing policy, section/overall scoring, interpretation and selector separation all exist and are tested across several modules.

namedTests.name: the written-out arithmetic is the trace's own aggregate, for every aggregate that has one

independentVerification.note: Scoring.explain returns outcome and trace from one evaluation; the named test checks the written-out numerator/denominator against the trace aggregate over 200 random cases (it asserts more than 150 were checked). The custom expression language is a closed DU and errors are typed NotScored outcomes. §§23-24 are mostly 'should' guidance.

namedTests.name: a custom expression equal to a built-in gives the same result (differential, 1000 samples)

gaps: §31 open questions are answered by DF-SIGNAL-2026-0002 (proposed answers), not by characterization of the Agile/Scrum Master 360 legacy formulas, which are not in this repository
independentVerification.note: End-to-end flow (decode -> typed template -> standard/custom scoring -> SurveyResult -> interpretation/diagnostics) exists; the 1000-sample differential of custom vs built-in would fail on interpreter regression.

namedTests.name: declaring ranking and allocation is accepted, and a capability the engine lacks is still refused

gaps: Selector presets are written to the canonical form by name (TemplateCanonical.fs:238). Answer options, scores and labels are embedded, so scoring is self-contained, but preset rendering still resolves from the engine's catalog.
independentVerification.note: Lineage, schema and engine version, and explicit COMPAT-CAPABILITY refusal of unsupported capabilities are implemented. Capabilities are also derived from content (RuleChecks.fs:101). The named test would fail if supported capabilities were refused or if unsupported ones were accepted.

namedTests.name: replaying a batch is idempotent and accepts nothing twice

gaps: Optional administrator-side revision tracking (PreviousImportedSubmissionHash, RevisionNumber) not implemented; URLC-002 makes it optional
Only one import policy (detect duplicate / reject different artifact) exists; the alternative policies are 'may' in URLC-002
independentVerification.note: As modified by URLC-002, replay is idempotent and a different artifact for an accepted instance is rejected (immutable-by-default), with durable tests asserting no extra commits on replay.

namedTests.name: a rule blocker fails the Rules category and nothing else

gaps: §22 Flow 'No unreachable required content' is checked only for an unconditional (When = Always) Hide of a required question or section (RuleChecks.fs:331-334). An unconditional Terminate or Skip over required content, or contradictory conditions, is not detected. ARX-010 static analysis is recorded as missing.
The named test covers only the Rules category of the summary. Coverage of the other gates relies on the CAN-005 tests.
independentVerification.note: Most §22 gates have stable codes (STRUCT-*, ANSWER-*, RULE-*, SCORING-*, COMPAT-*, ENCODING-*), and version uniqueness holds by construction (Publication.nextVersion). The reachability gate is shallow. §§23-25 fields are 'consider' items.

namedTests.name: group completion is explicit: required members and role minimums

gaps: The gap row's 15-invariant recheck omits invariant 7 (randomization must not make interpretation ambiguous); it is in fact covered by seeded bank selection (DF-SIGNAL-2026-0009, TimerBankTests:141) but the record does not cite it
Named test covers only invariants 9/11; the rest rely on tests in other modules
independentVerification.note: Cross-cutting invariants are each backed by some module test; the named test is narrow but real.

namedTests.name: a small state travels in the URL; a large one is stored and referenced

gaps: §§53-56 (resume from the decoded URL state; accepted identity set in the state) are replaced by DF-SIGNAL-2026-0004: resume and duplicate prevention read the store instead. The decision exists and says this.
independentVerification.note: Persistence is chosen by size with a safety margin, uses an opaque content-derived id, and refuses tampered, wrong-group and unknown references. Each of these is asserted with specific error cases.

namedTests.name: rejected and blocked artifacts never reach results, and leave only codes

gaps: §58 GroupAlreadyComplete error and §60 'additional imports should not be accepted ... Default: reject' are not implemented: ImportError has no such case and evaluateAgainst never compares accepted count to ExpectedCount; completion is 'accepted >= expected' (GroupResult.fs:153), so over-completion is silently accepted
Core invariant 4 ('AcceptedSurveyCount cannot exceed ExpectedSurveyCount by default') therefore does not hold and is untested
No DF-SIGNAL decision narrows this
independentVerification.note: Typed import errors, wrong-group/mode enforcement and 'rejected changes nothing' are implemented and tested, but the default rejection of imports into an already-complete group is missing.

namedTests.name: the report state is a deterministic projection of the group result

independentVerification.note: The report state is a projection of the incremental accumulator and equals a re-projection. Small states embed in the URL and large ones go to an external reference, and the test shows both paths return the same canonical state.

namedTests.name: a translation of something the template has passes; anything else is a blocker

independentVerification.note: Normative MUSTs (explicit unsupported-capability failure, deterministic randomization, N/A section not zero, distinct special states never zero) are implemented; remaining Localization/AccessibilityMetadata gaps were closed under DF-SIGNAL-2026-0020 with a test.

namedTests.name: format 2 carries the locale and the expiry day, and round-trips

gaps: §16 asks that the fingerprint length be 'chosen deliberately based on collision risk'. No written collision-risk rationale for the 8-byte reference was found in src, docs or research (process 'should', minor).
independentVerification.note: The instance carries opaque instance and group ids, the exact template reference, locale and expiry, all inside the integrity-checked envelope. Groups model roles, required members, dependencies and completion rules.

namedTests.name: an answer the link cannot carry blocks publication

gaps: No explicit reason code for 'TemplateVersion valid and unique' beyond Publication's identical-content/parent checks (Publication.fs:125-127); minor
independentVerification.note: Reason codes exist for every §28 gate family (STRUCT-*, ANSWER-*, RULE-*, SCORING-*, EXPR-*, COMPAT-*, ENCODING-*), and Publication.publish implements the §29 sequence; the named test meaningfully asserts the encoding round-trip blocker.

namedTests.name: every shipped, sample and demo template carries every answer state through the link

gaps: The named test covers only invariant 25. It sweeps every shipped template's states, but samples about 68 indices when a primitive has more than 96 values. I spot-checked invariants 22 and 25 only; the other 23 rely on the evidence the gap analysis cites (AuthoringTests, RulesTests, ScoringAstTests and so on).
independentVerification.note: The decode-validate-score pipeline exists and the spot-checked invariants hold with meaningful tests. I did not independently re-check all 25 invariants within the budget.

namedTests.name: each answer requests one history replace whose URL carries exactly the session

independentVerification.note: Test asserts exactly one Navigation effect with operation=replace and the exact fragment URL, and that resume reproduces answers/view/scores; source is SHOULD-level and fully covered.

namedTests.name: an anonymous response gets a fresh id and loses its instance, byte for byte

gaps: The named test exercises the pilot path (Submission.finalize). The generic path (GenericSession.finalOf) is covered more thinly, by SurveyPageTests:356.
Timer start and submit minutes survive anonymous finalization; DF-SIGNAL-2026-0010/0015 accept this explicitly as non-linking.
independentVerification.note: Finalization validates completion, draws a fresh id from entropy, refuses entropy equal to the instance or group id, and checks byte-for-byte that no instance bytes remain. Identified finalization keeps the instance and group.

namedTests.name: the group result does not depend on import order

independentVerification.note: Pipeline (parse/resolve/verify/decode/validate/score), derived group state, embedded-vs-external escalation and duplicate-instance rejection are implemented; order-independence test shuffles 20 times against a reference.

namedTests.name: an administrator creates a group, imports into it, and finalization waits for its obligations

gaps: §35 req 21 ('Real-time URL updates must be performant enough to occur on normal answer changes') has no test or benchmark. There is no Stopwatch or timing assertion anywhere in tests/.
The row says the lifecycle 'depends on LURL-001 through LURL-004', but LURL-004 is itself recorded as partial (incremental evaluation remains), so a group that depends on it should not be 'tested'.
independentVerification.note: Respondent-side history replace, resume and anonymous finalization, and the admin-side import, aggregation and report-state persistence, are all exercised. The performance requirement is unverified.

namedTests.name: every primitive round-trips through the URL for every binding (500 seeded samples)

independentVerification.note: Answers live only in the envelope with template-carried meaning; special states stay distinct in encoding and scoring (never zero by default).

namedTests.name: every selector preset fits its primitive and maps to a component family

independentVerification.note: Every listed preset exists over a reusable primitive, and maturity labels come from the template. The named test enumerates every union case by reflection and asserts that each one fits a primitive and has a component family.

namedTests.name: item scales: reverse within bounds and explicit maps

gaps: Multi-Select Aggregate: 'Maximum selected value' and 'Minimum selected value' strategies do not exist (MultiKey has ExactSetMatch/AnyCorrect/AllRequired/NoneForbidden/PartialCredit/OptionWeighted/CountSelected only, Keyed.fs:66-73)
'Explicit combination mapping' (mapping combinations to scores) is only approximated by single-set ExactSetMatch
independentVerification.note: Direct, reverse, binary/mapped, weighted, section aggregates and normalization are implemented and tested; two of the five named multi-select strategies are absent.

namedTests.name: an anonymous submission is accepted and scored exactly as the respondent saw it

gaps: Scoring is declared per section (one ItemScale per scorer), not per question. A single reverse-scored question in a mixed section needs a custom expression or a separate section. This is acceptable but coarser than the source's per-question example.
independentVerification.note: Scoring is never inferred from the selector: SectionScoring.Scorer must declare Direct, Reverse or Mapped, and Compatibility checks it. The named test checks the decode-to-score pipeline on the pilot.

namedTests.name: basic aggregates

independentVerification.note: All twelve algorithms have catalog implementations with concrete numeric assertions (raw sum, mean, weighted, % of max, normalize, mapped, reverse, banding, pass/fail, section/profile).

namedTests.name: through the console page each area is authored

gaps: The §5 'Reporting' area is not authored inside the template workspace. Report definitions are separate admin artifacts (ReportStore). The source lists this area only as recommended.
independentVerification.note: The lifecycle, versioning on publish, parent lineage and console authoring areas are implemented. No PII holds by construction: there is no free-text answer primitive.

namedTests.name: through the page the draft is previewed, scored live, kept as a fixture, and nothing is stored or sent

gaps: §26 lists Coverage as an assertable expected result; the Assertion type (Drafts.fs:20-33) has no coverage assertion (confidence is scoped out by DF-SIGNAL-2026-0025, coverage is not)
§28 capacity diagnostics: Layout.Capacity has no separate special-state bits or remaining-budget field (Layout.fs:127-133); soft 'such as' list
independentVerification.note: Preview through the real page engine, isolation (no commits), scoring/rule traces, fixtures blocking publication and PII-like warnings are implemented and tested; coverage cannot be asserted by a fixture.

namedTests.name: each interpretation check reports its own code

gaps: §34 'No permanently unreachable required content' and 'No impossible completion paths' are not implemented beyond an unconditional Hide of required content (RuleChecks.fs:331-334). Always-true Terminate or Skip past required questions, and unsatisfiable conditions, pass validation. ARX-010 (reachability analysis) is 'missing' in the gap analysis.
The named test exercises only interpretation checks, not the §32-§43 breadth the row claims.
independentVerification.note: Structural, answer, scoring, compatibility, encoding (including the fixture round trip), privacy and canonicalization-preview checks exist with codes. Flow reachability and completion-path validation are shallow.

namedTests.name: each interpretation field is classified: what decides the outcome is not comparable, labels and order are a caution
a relabel on any option primitive is a caution, never answer-changed and never silent

gaps: §50 blocker 'Broken anonymous unlinkability' has no template-validation code; it holds by construction (opaque ids, fresh anonymous id at finalization, tested under AUT-007/ID-002) rather than as a publication check
independentVerification.note: Diff kinds, comparability classes, per-category summary, blockers vs acknowledged warnings and immutable publication are implemented and tested.

namedTests.name: a stored draft and its review are deleted in one commit, and a published version is refused with its reason
through the page a fixture's scoring is explained, line by line (AUT-006 section 63)

gaps: §62 cross-device checks for real WebKit and Firefox run only in a scheduled workflow outside PR checks (DF-SIGNAL-2026-0016), so a regression there is not caught by the PR suite.
independentVerification.note: Supersession without removal, rollback as a new version, hiding, the test manifest, provenance kept outside the hash, test-mode refusal on production import, and the fixture explanation are each asserted.

namedTests.name: an anonymous response gets a fresh id and loses its instance, byte for byte

gaps: Invariant 19 ('Anonymous unlinkability is validated before publication') is enforced as an engine-wide runtime guarantee at finalization (Submission.fs:48-78), not as a per-template publication check; acceptable only because unlinkability does not depend on template content
independentVerification.note: The named test meaningfully asserts the instance id is absent from the encoded anonymous submission; the other invariants map to tested modules cited in the WI-0081 recheck.

namedTests.name: the state is in the fragment, never the path or query

independentVerification.note: The URL fragment is the transport and resume state. The deletions hold by construction, since there is no server respondent state. Duplicates are an import concern: ImportTests checks idempotent re-import.

namedTests.name: a submitted session is sealed, and reopening a submission shows it sealed

independentVerification.note: Live response vs sealed portable submission, derived instance status, integrity checksum (IntegrityFailed / TemplateMismatch on decode), exact template reference and group id in submission are all tested.

namedTests.name: every single-byte corruption and every truncation is detected

gaps: §8 keyed-signature authenticity is not implemented. The code documents the envelope as integrity-only (UrlState.fs:30), which the source allows ('may later').
independentVerification.note: DecodeError covers each §6 case. The named test flips every byte and tries every truncation, and asserts that each is detected.

namedTests.name: after every message the page can send, the link decodes to exactly the response

independentVerification.note: The envelope carries template reference, instance/group binding, answers, encoding version and integrity check; the property test over 60 seeds x templates asserts link decode equals session response.

namedTests.name: a retained URL artifact and its exact template reconstruct the stored result (URLC-005)

independentVerification.note: A retained artifact plus its exact template reproduces the stored result, and a different template does not. A group that does not retain artifacts reports NotRetained.

namedTests.name: an identified response keeps its instance and group

independentVerification.note: Opaque instance/group ids, invitation bound to exact template version, identified submission keeps instance+group; no person fields exist.

namedTests.name: the same response finalized twice is not linkable: the id comes only from entropy

independentVerification.note: The anonymous id comes only from entropy and the group is kept. The identified and anonymous shapes are distinct binding cases, and no PII primitive exists. The same evidence base as LURL-002.

namedTests.name: a small anonymous group shows counts but suppresses score aggregates

independentVerification.note: Expected/accepted/missing counts, dedup by identity+SubmissionHash, anonymous conversion with payload check, entropy tests (1000 distinct draws, no stuck bits) and anonymous suppression are implemented and asserted.

namedTests.name: anonymous groups count contributions and refuse instance-level rules

independentVerification.note: Anonymous finalization drops the instance id and takes a fresh id from entropy only. Entropy equal to the instance or group id is refused. Anonymous groups count contributions and refuse instance-level completion rules.

namedTests.name: the SDRA pilot validates and publishes as version 1

independentVerification.note: Stable SurveyIdentifier, version assigned at publication, deterministic TemplateHash (golden value pinned in ScoringAstTests:257), instances reference the exact version.

namedTests.name: publication assigns versions, supersedes without removing, and locks the hash

independentVerification.note: The named test asserts that unchanged content is refused, versions are derived, superseded versions stay resolvable by version, hash and reference, provenance does not affect the hash, and a tampered artifact fails verify.

namedTests.name: format 2 carries the locale and the expiry day, and round-trips

gaps: CreatedAt and a Cancelled status are not carried; the source lists them as 'potential' fields and URLC-001/002 remove server-side status
independentVerification.note: Runtime policy fields (resume, back navigation, changes-after-completion default false, show results, result mode), derived status and locale/expiry carriage in integrity-checked link format 2 are implemented and tested.

namedTests.name: a template that asks for a review shows every answer before it is submitted, and only then submits

independentVerification.note: Items per page (survey and section), page breaks, sections on a new page, numbering, progress modes and review-before-submit are implemented and tested. Randomization is an optional 'potential' feature and is fixed off, which is the source's default.

namedTests.name: pagination follows items per page, section overrides, breaks and new-page sections

gaps: Invariant 14 (pagination must not affect scoring) is asserted via layout-fingerprint equality, not by comparing scores directly
independentVerification.note: Named test checks pagination and that paging leaves the encoding layout unchanged; other invariants are covered by Rules/Paging/Resolution tests.

namedTests.name: a state that fits travels in the URL; one that does not is read, written once, and an unknown write is reconciled

gaps: 'Capabilities MUST be derived from authoritative state': SessionStates, FinalizationStates, BatchStates and TemplateStates are not referenced by any production code in src. They are parallel test-facing models. The real reducers (for example GenericSession.update, per SessionStates.fs:7) do not consult them. Only ReportStates (GroupStore) and GroupLifecycle drive production behaviour.
FinalizationStates wraps the pilot Submission.finalize, not the generic survey path (GenericSession.finalOf).
Guards are not a distinct element of the shared System shape (only Requires plus Attempt).
independentVerification.note: The shared shape (illegal-transition results, capability vocabulary, obligations with discharge evidence, Unknown/SearchedNotFound knowledge) exists, and all seven systems are expressed in it. For four of the seven, the models are not the authority the application runs on.

namedTests.name: an unknown outcome that landed is reconciled, not imported twice

gaps: 'Administrator import MUST be modeled as a state machine' with pre-acceptance states (Parsing, ResolvingTemplate, Verifying, ...ReadyToAccept): import is a single pure pipeline function returning Accepted/AlreadyImported/Rejected; stages appear only as a derived evidence string list (Intake.fs:72-73), not as modeled states/transitions

The OutcomeUnknown path that does NOT resolve (reconciliation-required state, retry withheld) is implemented (GroupStore.fs:341) but no import test exercises it; only the 'landed' case is tested in DurableImportTests:135 (OutcomeUnknownLost is tested only for roster changes, AdminStoreTests:279)
independentVerification.note: Idempotency, optimistic concurrency and landed-unknown reconciliation are real and tested; the explicit pre-acceptance state machine and the still-unknown import branch are not evidenced.

namedTests.name: wording that asks for identity is found in every author-written text, and blocks by policy

gaps: The differencing ledger's handling of filtered or subgroup views (View.Filters) is exercised only in the pure PrivacyTests. Every runtime caller records only unfiltered whole-group counts (Disclosure.fs:167, ReportLibrary.fs:225).
Role breakdowns are all-or-nothing within one release but are not entered in the ledger. Role counts across successive released snapshots are therefore not checked for differencing.
No test addresses 'before/after comparisons' as a differencing path at runtime.
independentVerification.note: PII injection fixtures, unknown-field refusal, query stripping and answer-free diagnostics are solid. Multi-view differencing protection is implemented for whole-group snapshots and live releases, but only partly for subgroup and role views.

namedTests.name: a value traces back through the path that computed it, without identities

gaps: SurveyResult lineage lacks SemanticHash, ExecutionPlanHash and SurveyResultHash; no grep hit for any of these or ReportSnapshotHash in src/
Report-snapshot lineage (ReportDefinitionHash, localization hash, ReportSnapshotHash) not evidenced

Trial-metrics MUST (distinguish zero/unknown/unavailable/not-collected, no fabricated telemetry) lives in Praxis tooling (docs/development-telemetry.md:56,85), not exercised by any Signal test cited for this group
independentVerification.note: Group lineage + trace and single-path explanations (Scoring.Trace) are real and tested; the lineage manifest items and the trial-metrics clause are not covered by the claim.

namedTests.name: an expired question timer holds only its question, and the page names it

gaps: 'The template MUST also support section banks': only question banks exist (Banking.Bank pools question ids; Template.Banks). There is no section-bank type, so the 'publisher MUST reject section-bank definitions whose dependencies cannot be satisfied' check is also absent. No DF decision narrows this.
'Clock unavailability or invalid clock evidence MUST produce an explicit state/error': no such state was found in src.
The combined stress-trial fixture (timed + adaptive + banked, exercising Clock, Entropy, Navigation and Clipboard) was not identified.
independentVerification.note: Pagination, independent revisit locks, Back/Forward enforcement, versioned seeded question-bank selection (DF-0009) and survey, section, page and question timers are implemented and tested. Section banking is missing.

namedTests.name: the GitHub provider and the in-memory provider state the same knowledge

gaps: Named test only compares two capability tables (ProviderTests.fs:66-67) and would not catch a configuration/layout/credential regression; StorageTests and AdminStoreTests carry the real evidence
independentVerification.note: Configurable owner/branch/base path, no-credential-written check, versioned storage manifest, capability verification and read-only mode on read-only credentials are implemented and tested.

namedTests.name: the storage manifest names the dataset, its folder and every format version

independentVerification.note: The manifest holds versions and no PII (exact key-set assertion). Future versions, other datasets, tampering and mid-migration stores each fail explicitly. The SHOULD fields are present or split with Arca's manifest.

namedTests.name: the survey domain names no repository, branch, commit or path concept

gaps: Name-scan test covers only the Engine assembly; AdminReportState (Admin assembly, which references Arca) is clean on inspection but not under test
independentVerification.note: Engine references no Arca/GitHub assembly and names no repository/branch/commit/sha; GitHub's missing capabilities (transactions, server-side query/aggregate, streaming) are discovered as Unavailable.

namedTests.name: concurrent imports of distinct submissions commute; the same identity is decided again

independentVerification.note: The identity-keyed record path makes a retry a duplicate. Concurrent distinct imports both land, and a stale same-identity import is re-decided as a duplicate. An unknown outcome that landed is reconciled without a second import.

namedTests.name: contributions are immutable records sharded by identity, and no raw URL is kept

gaps: Current aggregate is never persisted (recomputed from contributions on open), so 'detect a stale aggregate' is satisfied by construction rather than by a detection mechanism
independentVerification.note: Immutable sharded result records, a rebuildable index with stale detection, derivation hashes and verified report snapshots are implemented and tested.

namedTests.name: incremental aggregation equals full recomputation for every prefix of random sequences

gaps: Incremental aggregation is built on the pilot Assessment dimensions. The random-sequence test uses the pilot only (Generic = None).
independentVerification.note: The test runs 25 random sequences and compares incremental and full results at every prefix, plus commutativity, idempotence and refusal of conflicting identities. The accumulator keeps sorted evidence rather than rescanning history.

namedTests.name: descriptive measures come from the evidence and say how they were computed

independentVerification.note: Measures, canonical-vs-calculated separation ('analysis never changes the canonical result'), and a versioned, depth-bounded, I/O-free AnalysisExpression all asserted.

namedTests.name: comparison rests on semantics, and refuses with reasons when they differ

independentVerification.note: NotComparable is returned with reason codes for survey, identity mode, privacy policy, and a template difference without a declaration. A versioned continuity declaration is validated. Comparison is a pure function and does not mutate results.

namedTests.name: every chart type declares its legal shapes, and invalid combinations fail

gaps: SHOULD-level chart types needing a second dimension (grouped/stacked bar, heatmap, box plot, matrix, small multiples) are refused rather than supported
independentVerification.note: All MUSTs (F#-validated semantics, declared legal shapes, invalid combinations fail) are met and asserted with specific refusal values.

namedTests.name: sorting is deterministic and a truncated bar axis is warned

independentVerification.note: Each listed suitability rule has a refusal or warning that is asserted: line/ordered, histogram, stack denominator, more than 12 categories, truncated axis, deterministic sort, missing never zero, totals withheld, non-colour encodings, stable legend. The unit type distinguishes 0-1 from 0-100.

namedTests.name: every chart has a description, a table and non-colour encodings with enough contrast

gaps: The accessibility validator's rejection codes (LOW_CONTRAST, COLOUR_ONLY_DISTINCTION, NO_DESCRIPTION, TABLE_DIFFERS_FROM_CHART) are never asserted to fire; the named test only checks it returns empty for a good chart, so a validator that always returns [] would pass
'Touch targets suitable for mobile/tablet' and 'zoom/reflow support' (minimum list) have no implementation evidence or test
High-contrast support is a single forced-colors CSS rule (admin.css:14) with no test
independentVerification.note: Description, table equivalence, palette contrast >=3:1 and distinct pattern/symbol per colour are genuinely asserted; the validation pass and several minimum items are untested.

namedTests.name: an administrator creates a group, imports into it, and finalization waits for its obligations

gaps: No assertion checks that exploration leaves stored results unchanged (MUST NOT alter canonical results). It holds structurally, but no test would catch a regression.
independentVerification.note: The named test's exploration block drills into a section's distribution, toggles percentages, holds the analysis in the URL, and restores it on LocationChanged.

namedTests.name: a value traces back through the path that computed it, without identities

gaps: SHOULD fields ReportDefinitionVersion, VisualizationSpecVersion and snapshot identity are not in Trace; trace covers section statistics only, not chart points or recommendation frequency
independentVerification.note: MUSTs met: trace derives from the same Incremental.result path (derivation hash asserted equal), exposes only submission hashes, and reports suppression codes for small anonymous groups.

namedTests.name: views whose populations nest and differ by fewer than the minimum are not both released

gaps: Same caveat as ARX-009: runtime ledger entries are unfiltered views only. The admin analysis 'Filter' is a group-list filter, not a contribution filter, so interactive subgroup filtering of anonymous contributions does not appear to exist.
independentVerification.note: Minimum sizes, complementary suppression, distribution minima and the release ledger are decided before ReportData is produced. The differencing SHOULD is met for the views the console actually offers.

namedTests.name: tampered, truncated, oversized and future records are held aside with typed reasons
a canonical edit of a record's body is detected and the record held aside, never loaded as authentic (SEC-01)
a canonical hand edit that escalates an administrator is detected on load, never trusted (SEC-01)

gaps: 'MUST detect tampering': the 'tampered' case (LoadingTests.fs:142) is only a non-canonical whitespace edit; a canonical edit of a record body (changed value) is not detected because Loading computes ContentHash but never compares it to an expected hash (Arca's Integrity.unchanged is unused anywhere in src/)
Manifests do not reference child object hashes (SHOULD)
independentVerification.note: Truncation, wrong schema, misplaced and wrong-dataset records are detected and tested, and exports exclude locators; semantic tampering of a mutable record is not detectable or tested.

namedTests.name: the contribution index is rebuilt from the records, detected stale, and rebuilt the same

gaps: A corrupt (as opposed to stale or missing) index is not exercised by a test. 'Derived.compare rebuilt rebuilt' at the end of the named test is tautological.
independentVerification.note: Validate, rebuild and compare are implemented. The test asserts Missing -> Current -> Stale after a new import, and a deterministic rebuild.

namedTests.name: audit records hold opaque ids, hashes and codes, and refuse anything personal

independentVerification.note: Audit records accept only opaque ids, hashes and UPPER-KEBAB codes; the test asserts concrete refusals for login, name, e-mail, URL and token values.

namedTests.name: analysis state travels in the URL with integrity, and saved analyses are records

gaps: The 'free of credentials' assertion is weak: it only checks that the fragment does not contain the string 'token'. Credential-freedom rests mainly on the declarative type and on Arca refusing credential-like content.
independentVerification.note: Search and filtering use non-PII group fields only (all SHOULD). Saved analyses are declarative, versioned records with integrity-checked URL state.

namedTests.name: offline the page stays readable, says it may be stale, and withholds every change

gaps: The offline test asserts the notice code and capability removal but not the rendered last-verified time
independentVerification.note: Read-only credentials/protected branches open read-only with writes removed from authoritative capabilities; offline enters degraded mode with an explicit 'may be out of date' notice.

namedTests.name: a malformed message is an Aegis fault, and an unknown event fails loud

gaps: The named test is narrow (malformed message -> fault; unknown event throws). The boundary is evidenced mostly by the tiny browser JS and the claimed 'limen verify --strict' CI step, which was not run here.
independentVerification.note: The admin browser code is 11 lines plus a 102-line host pack, so business logic cannot live in TypeScript or JS. All state, commands and decisions are F#.

namedTests.name: a template upgrade explains what continues and what a saved analysis loses

gaps: Dependencies.preview/obligations have no production caller anywhere in src/ (grep finds no use outside Dependencies.fs), so no administrator change actually computes or presents an impact preview or creates obligations before applying

Change kinds cover only 7 cases (Dependencies.fs:89-96); group-configuration, report-definition, dashboard, visualization, comparison-policy, storage-schema and aggregate-schema changes are not modeled
Named test exercises Dependencies.upgrade (template diff), not the impact preview; the preview is tested in AnalyticsTests:193
independentVerification.note: The classifier with reason codes and evidence exists and is unit-tested, but it is a library not wired into any change flow.

namedTests.name: retiring a finalized group's results removes them from Signal's state and the current tree, claims no more, and records the limit
the dataset moves through its lifecycle, read-only while not active, and verified provider deletion is never offered

gaps: 'Archival MUST preserve enough lineage to reproduce formal snapshots that are intentionally retained' has no direct test. Archived is only a lifecycle state, and nothing shows snapshot reproduction after archival or retirement.
independentVerification.note: Nine lifecycle states with legal, audited transitions. Claims distinguish application state, current tree and history, and are never 'permanent'. A retired dataset is read-only.

namedTests.name: a stored template whose expression exceeds the limits is a problem, never a template (ADM-046)
a record stored without its body hash is refused, so removing the hash does not bypass the check (SEC-01)

gaps: 'Content hash' validation: generic records' hash is computed, not checked against any expected value (only published templates re-verify their template hash, TemplateRecord.fs:261)
'Cross-object version compatibility' has no identifiable check or test
independentVerification.note: Staged loading with typed codes for path, size, schema, canonical encoding, dataset, type, duplicates, references, cycles, partial listing and expression/dashboard limits is real and tested.

namedTests.name: every roster change can be undone by a new change

gaps: Undo is demonstrated for roster changes only. Report-definition and dashboard reverts are SHOULD-level and are not shown by the named test.
independentVerification.note: Undo is a new inverse command, asserted to restore capabilities. Refusals carry stable codes (Access.explain). The group is mostly SHOULD-level.

namedTests.name: recomputing only the invalidated closure equals a full rebuild

gaps: The dependency graph is not used by any production code (no caller of Dependencies.* in src/), so it does not power incremental recomputation, staleness, repair or lineage as the SHOULDs describe

Named test is near-tautological: the closure of g/contributions contains every measure, and the 'incremental' map recomputes those from the full post-change source, so it equals the full rebuild by construction (AnalyticsTests.fs:235-242); it would not catch an incremental-path regression
independentVerification.note: An explicit graph and closure function exist and the closure test is meaningful, but the incremental==full claim is not genuinely proven and the graph is not wired in.

namedTests.name: two artifacts claiming the same survey and version conflict, and neither is used

independentVerification.note: A dedicated resolver with priority-ordered registries and a verified cache. It distinguishes not-found (scoped to what was searched), unavailable or unauthorized, hash mismatch, conflict, unsupported and cached outcomes, and never substitutes another version.

namedTests.name: the credential's state distinguishes every case ADM-056 names

independentVerification.note: Every named credential state is distinguished, capabilities are recomputed from state, and a locator resolving to another repository is refused pending administrator resolution.

namedTests.name: a dataset in its own profile lives in that profile's repository

gaps: The gap row's 'Tests: ProviderTests' does not match its named test, which lives in StorageTests (bookkeeping only).
independentVerification.note: A label is presentation only (relabelling moves nothing), and an edited location is refused as needing a migration. A profile cannot be removed while a dataset lives in it (deployment parse error, tested at StorageTests:111).

namedTests.name: an interrupted batch resumes where it stopped and counts nothing twice

independentVerification.note: Stable batch id, per-item outcomes, every listed BatchStatus, resume after a simulated mid-batch network loss without double counting, and cancellation keeping committed work are asserted.

namedTests.name: deleting accepted results limits reproduction to aggregates and records why

independentVerification.note: Reconstruction levels are derived from what is held. Each deletion enumerates the breaks, closes lineage and writes a PII-free audit limitation, which the runtime retirement persists and reads back.

namedTests.name: only legal transitions apply; a sealed group is never reopened

gaps: No store-level test that an import into a Sealed group is refused; only the predicate acceptsContributions Sealed=false and the page's canImport flag are asserted
independentVerification.note: Sealed accepts no contributions or configuration, cannot be reopened, and can only be superseded; the predicate is wired into GroupStore and AdminGroupWork.

namedTests.name: an import writes its audit records in the same commit, naming artifacts by hash only

gaps: The test scans only audit records for person identifiers, not contribution records. Contribution Provenance has no person field by construction (ResultRecord.fs:60-65).
independentVerification.note: Provenance is {Origin, BatchId, ArtifactHash, EncodingVersion}. The audit records are asserted to contain only hashes, with no login, account number or URL.

namedTests.name: offline, nothing is queued: the change fails and nothing is written later

independentVerification.note: Offline mutations fail with nothing written later, unknown outcomes are reconciled, and the page test asserts offline flag, stale indication and withheld actions.

namedTests.name: memory-only is the default: no token is stored anywhere in the browser

independentVerification.note: Memory-only is the default, tab scope is opt-in, and persistent storage is never offered. Tests assert the tokens appear nowhere in tab or device storage, navigations, addresses or broadcasts, and that faults carry no token.

namedTests.name: another tab's sign-out ends this tab's session

independentVerification.note: Notices only downgrade, and a stale tab's command is still conditioned on the provider change token and re-decided (the sole MUST).

namedTests.name: a read-only credential or a protected branch opens the dataset read-only

gaps: Branch-protection detection itself comes from Arca's CapabilitySnapshot (an external library), which was not inspected. The refusal code for a protected branch is the generic 'CredentialValidReadOnly' rather than ProtectedBranchRequiresReview.
independentVerification.note: All six write modes are distinguished. The test asserts that both a read-only credential and a protected branch open the dataset read-only, and that a change is refused before any write.

namedTests.name: every stored record refuses a field for identity

gaps: Catalog completeness itself is evidenced by the SCS-002..013 groups, not by this group's named test
independentVerification.note: No text/contact/upload/location selector kind exists and stored records refuse identity fields; the boundary is tested.

namedTests.name: basic aggregates

gaps: CountMatching ('counts conditions, choices, or answer-key matches that satisfy a declared predicate') has no stable named built-in. Only CountAtLeast (a >= threshold predicate) and answer keys exist; counting declared rule conditions needs a custom expression. Neither the gap analysis nor a decision accounts for it.
'Unscored' exists only implicitly, as the absence of section Scoring.
independentVerification.note: Almost the whole catalog is present and tested with concrete values (including the even-median rule, the usable-item denominator and banding validation). CountMatching is the unaccounted item.

namedTests.name: box, favorable and NPS metrics

gaps: 'Favorability MUST follow declared option semantics/direction': Top/Bottom-box and favorable presets take only numeric cutoffs/maximum and assume higher value = favorable (Registry.fs:62-75); there is no declared-direction parameter
No test combines a Reverse scale with TopKBox/favorable metrics to show reversal precedes aggregate metrics (MUST)
independentVerification.note: All named presets exist and compile to catalog scorers with correct numeric results; the two direction/reversal MUSTs are not demonstrated.

namedTests.name: ranking methods are deterministic by position and item count

gaps: Pairwise WinCount, WeightedWinCount and WinLossDifference, and normalized best-minus-worst, exist only as library functions (Keyed.fs:197-225). Nothing in src calls them, and there is no template item key for them. Template.keyedNumber wires only RankKeyed, AllocationKeyed and per-question BestWorst indicators. A template therefore cannot select these methods without a custom expression, and the expression language has no such operator. This conflicts with 'basic count/difference scoring MUST not require a custom expression'.
independentVerification.note: The ranking methods (including Borda by position and count, and TopK equal or positional credit) and all five allocation methods with explicit zero totals are implemented, reachable from templates and tested. The pairwise and normalized best-worst scorers are unit-tested library code only.

namedTests.name: benchmarks are versioned by content and never fabricate a norm

gaps: Benchmark has no caller outside Benchmark.fs (only a ReportModel enum case mentions benchmarks): a template cannot declare a benchmark and no SurveyResult produces norm scores, so 'support norm-referenced transformations without requiring custom expressions' is not reachable by authors
'TScore defaults only when the template explicitly selects the conventional transform' cannot be honoured because no template field exists
independentVerification.note: The transforms and their MUST semantics (content hash, version recorded, tie policy, zero-SD error, no fabrication) are correct and tested at library level only.

namedTests.name: cardinalities are the documented counts

independentVerification.note: Every required primitive (including quantized BoundedNumber and BoundedRange) has a finite cardinality and a bijective index. Range low <= high is enforced, matrix is a composite, and Declined is a distinct special state.

namedTests.name: a selection the count refuses is held on the page with where it stands, and the link never carries it

independentVerification.note: Count rules and exclusive options with ClearOthers/RejectCombination are tested; the page states the count up front and the link never carries an invalid selection.

namedTests.name: a pairwise question is two keyboard choices on the page, its choice travels in the link, and the draft publishes

gaps: 'Allocation MUST support ... a visible remaining/assigned total': the survey page shows only the target ('Share N points between the options', GenericInputs.fs:72) and a generic 'Not in the link yet' error. SelectionGuidance.status gives a running count for multi-choice only, and no allocation running or remaining total was found in the view or tests.
independentVerification.note: Ranking by position number (no drag), numeric allocation with step and bounds, distinct best-worst, pairwise as two radios, and hierarchical single and multi with parent rules are implemented. The allocation running total is missing.

namedTests.name: every input names its question and says it is required; each question names its component

gaps: 'visible focus' and color-vision/low-vision requirements have no test evidence (no focus-outline or contrast assertions in tests/browser)
Keyboard operability is browser-tested only for radio-style selectors (ui-conformance-layout.spec.js:178-196), not for every selector family (e.g. ranking, allocation)
independentVerification.note: Accessible name, required/invalid state, error association, touch target, 400% reflow and reduced motion are tested; visible focus and colour/low-vision rules are unevidenced.

namedTests.name: selector-scorer incompatibilities block publication with a stable code

gaps: The Pairwise contract scorers (WinCount, WeightedWinCount, WinLossDifference) exist as functions in Keyed.fs:197-207, but KeyKind has no pairwise case, so a template cannot declare them and compatibility cannot accept them.
BoundedRange 'distance/overlap against a declared target range' is missing: RangeMeasure has only width, midpoint, low and high.
The BoundedInteger/Decimal 'Difference', 'Ratio' and 'Distance/Proximity' scorers have no declarable form.
independentVerification.note: Incompatible combinations do fail publication with the stable code SCORING-INCOMPATIBLE, and that is tested. Several combinations the contract lists as supported cannot be declared, so the contract is only partly realized.

namedTests.name: capacity is the length of the largest real envelope

independentVerification.note: Finite per-primitive cardinalities are asserted; capacity equals the largest real envelope, and over-budget templates are blocked (ENCODING-URL-BUDGET) rather than truncated.

namedTests.name: the written-out arithmetic is the trace's own aggregate, for every aggregate that has one

gaps: The per-response confidence sidecar is scoped out by DF-SIGNAL-2026-0025 (a group measure, WI-0059). The decision exists and says so. Fixture-coverage lists are SHOULD-level and were not audited item by item.
independentVerification.note: The preview explains raw answer, contribution, weight, reversal, key credit and penalty, numerator over denominator, bounds, bands and coverage from the evaluation trace. The named test property-checks that the written arithmetic matches the trace aggregate across 5 aggregates x 40 random answer sets.

gaps: StorageFaults has no production caller (only tests use it); in production GitHub failures are classified inside Arca's GitHub adapter, so the requirement is met by delegation rather than by Signal's own module
Gap-analysis row names no specific test
independentVerification.note: Signal does not call the GitHub API directly; it references the Aegis GitHub package and its GitHub calls go through Arca, which uses the Aegis failure model; status-to-code mapping is asserted in ProviderTests.

gaps: Authorization failure (403 without rate-limit headers) maps to AEGIS.GITHUB.AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. This is acceptable: the Aegis.Integration.GitHub 1.0.0 package exposes no separate authorization code, and the source says 'applicable cases exposed by the current Aegis GitHub integration'.
independentVerification.note: Each failure class (401/403, 404, primary and secondary rate limits, 504 and network, 502/503, malformed or 500) is asserted to a deterministic Aegis code. An uncertain write outcome is shown to go to reconciliation (AfterReconciling).

gaps: No test names SIG-LINK-005 (copy link) or SIG-LINK-010 (Limen router API) by id; coverage is indirect.
Not in WI-0100's independent verification sample.
